claims.claim: **Offer schistosomiasis serology to anyone who has lived in or travelled through an endemic area** (such as Africa, the Middle East and some of South East Asia). No follow-up is needed if serology is negative.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Why screen:** infection stays silent until late end-organ damage (portal hypertension, renal failure, bladder cancer), adult worms can survive 20–30 years after leaving an endemic area, and treatment is simple, safe and usually curative.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Serology is the screening test,** with stool or urine microscopy reserved for seropositive people. It stays positive after cure, so it cannot separate past from current infection, and it is less sensitive for *S. japonicum* and *S. mekongi*. Consider schistosomiasis in unexplained eosinophilia after time in an endemic area.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If serology is positive or equivocal, give praziquantel 40 mg/kg orally as two doses of 20 mg/kg four hours apart, with no upper dose limit** (evidence grade A).
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The same 40 mg/kg dose is advised whatever the region of origin;** the older 60 mg/kg regimen for Asian-acquired infection rested on weak evidence, and a randomised trial found 40 mg/kg equally effective.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Praziquantel is PBS-listed for schistosomiasis as a streamlined authority** for doctors and nurse practitioners. The 600 mg tablet splits into quarters, so doses can be rounded to the nearest 150 mg.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild side effects affect 5–30%** (nausea, dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, itch), possibly a reaction to dying worms. Routine brain imaging for neurocysticercosis is not needed, but a person with unexplained seizures needs fundoscopy and brain imaging, and suspected neurocysticercosis needs ID review before praziquantel.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After positive serology, check stool for ova, and urine dipstick for blood; send end-urine for ova only if there is haematuria.** Ova in stool or urine mean further work-up with ultrasound and LFTs.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S. mansoni with any feature of liver impairment:** liver ultrasound to exclude pipe-stem fibrosis, and refer to an ID physician.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S. haematobium (ova in urine):** examine for genital disease and do a renal tract ultrasound; refer to urology for macroscopic haematuria, recurrent UTIs, abnormal imaging or genital disease.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recheck stool or urine for ova no sooner than 8 weeks after treatment; retreat if still positive, and refer to ID if ova persist beyond 8 weeks after a second course.** Do not repeat serology, which can stay positive for years; confirm the tablets were actually taken.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess and treat children like adults, but keep a low threshold for paediatric ID referral** (persisting eosinophilia or ova after one course), and seek specialist advice under 4 years, where safety data are thinner.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy (category B1):** withhold praziquantel for asymptomatic infection in the first trimester, then offer it later in pregnancy after discussion, or give it after delivery. Breastfeeding mothers can be treated.
claims.locator: Foundation House (Victorian Foundation for Survivors of Torture), Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide, 'Australian Refugee Health Practice Guide: Schistosomiasis (Davis JS, Phillips C, Clifford V)', last updated November 2018, https://refugeehealthguide.org.au/schistosomiasis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
